newsitem.title: CROATIA: Lawyer challenges demand for war crimes evidence.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer challenges demand for war crimes evidence.

text.p: A lawyer for a Bosnian Croat general indicted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal has challenged its demand for state evidence from Croatia.
The International War Crimes Tribunal for former Yugoslavia (ICTY) on Saturday set August 18 as the deadline for Croatia to provide information about General Tihomir Blaskic.
Croatia has refused to comply with the court's six-month-old subpoena,citing national security reasons.
Anto Nobilo, chief of Blaskic's defence team, told Croatian television on Saturday the request was illegal and made "in contradiction to the prevalent opinion of most legal experts".
The subpoena called on Croatia to hand over 13 categories of documents relating to the Blaskic case. Croatian officials have not commented on the ICTY's deadline.
The tribunal said it had powers to issue the subpoena and that states and their officials were obliged to comply.
Nobilo disagreed and said: "Only the Security Council can punish a sovereign country. The Tribunal has no mandate for that."

Croatia Sources said the documents included Blaskic's notes to the Croatian defence ministry, its records on arms supplies to Bosnian Croats and orders he received from the head of the Bosnian Croat separatist entity.
Blaskic, aged 36, is accused of directing a brutal ethnic cleansing campaign against Bosnian Moslems in 1993, when he was commander of Bosnian Croat militia (HVO) in Central Bosnia.
